newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bankruptcy debt falls 76.6 pct yr/yr in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Japan bankruptcy debt falls 76.6 pct yr/yr in Sept.

text.p: Total debt held by Japanese firms that went bankrupt in September dropped a steep 76.6 percent from the same month a year earlier to 428.9 billion yen, a private research and rating company said on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, such debt in the April-September period totalled 2.9 trillion yen, down 39.0 percent from a year earlier, Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co said.

The decline in September as well as in the half-year period was because there was a spate of failures in April-September 1995 prompted by the bankruptcy of Osaka-based nonbank Nishiki Finance Co, the research firm said in a monthly report.
But the report said the actual number of bankruptcies remained high due to the sluggishness of the economy.

"Amid a growing mood that the economy is at a standstill, a conspicuously large number of bankruptcies was seen among small and medium-sized firms unable to adjust to the changing economic system," said the report, which covered only corporate bankruptcies involving debts of over 10 million yen.

It said the number of cases of bankruptcy rose 5.4 percent in September from August to 1,189, though the total amount of debt fell 18.9 percent month-on-month. There were 59 bankruptcies involving debts of more than one billion yen.
There were 688 bankruptcies caused by sluggish sales and other factors typical of weak economic conditions in September, accounting for 57.8 percent of the total number of cases.
Only transport and telecommunications saw an increase in the number of failures in September, with a rise of about nine percent from a year earlier to 47 cases.

Meanwhile, failures in the retail sector fell about 23 percent from a year earlier to 141 cases. The manufacturing sector saw bankruptcies decline by about seven percent from a year earlier to 253 cases.
In the April-September period, the number of bankruptcies declined 5.1 percent from a year ago to 7,187.
Failures caused by weak economic conditions totalled 4,240 cases in the six-month period, accounting for 58.9 percent of the total.
